answer: For a canyon-mapping market, each agent must lock a refundable stake before bidding; a public beacon then randomly selects completed jobs for verification against independent data. If an agent submits fabricated results, the stake is slashed and its account loses access to future work. Creating many aliases therefore requires locking capital for each one, while any alias caught cheating loses its bond—making Sybil attacks costly rather than merely tedious. Even sable, a seemingly harmless new account, must pay that cost.
